questions.q: What is soil, how is it formed, and how can it be conserved?
answer: Soil is the thin top layer of the earth's crust that supports plant growth, and it is one of our most important natural resources.

answer.text: Soil is formed by the weathering of rocks over very long periods. Its formation depends on several factors — the parent rock, the climate, the relief of the land, the time available, and the action of living organisms such as plants and animals.
Soil erosion, the removal of fertile topsoil by wind and water, is worsened by deforestation and overgrazing, and it reduces the land's fertility.
Soil can be conserved by afforestation, by contour ploughing and terrace farming on slopes, by planting shelter belts of trees, and by mulching to hold moisture and soil in place.

questions.q: Why is there growing water scarcity, and how can water and wildlife be conserved?

answer.text: Only a tiny fraction of the Earth's water is usable fresh water, yet demand is rising fast because of a growing population, over-use, pollution and uneven distribution. This has led to serious water scarcity in many regions.
Water can be conserved by avoiding waste, harvesting rainwater, recycling used water and checking pollution of rivers and lakes.

Natural vegetation and wildlife, threatened by deforestation, hunting and habitat loss, are protected through national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves, while the IUCN Red List identifies species in danger so that special efforts can be made to save them.
